# dsh-memory-keeper

> Cross-session memory for DSH. Every session is exported to a
> readable Markdown transcript (dialo

gue only), one long-term `MEMORY.md` is kept as the main file, and a new window
> gets a compact wak
e-up summary instead of starting from nothing.
English | 中文
## What it is
`dsh-memory-keeper` gives an agent a memory that survives windows. It reads DSH's own session files

(read-only),
turns each conversation into plain Markdown with every message tagged by provenance, ke

eps a long-term `MEMORY.md`
that the agent writes to, and assembles a small "wake up" digest when a
fresh conversation begins.
## Why
DSH sessions are isolated. Open a new window and the previous conversation is simply gone from the a

gent's view —
only a compressed session file stays on disk, in a format meant for DSH itself, not fo

r reading. Long conversations
also get compacted, and details quietly fall out of context. So an age

nt that was told something last week has no
reliable way to remember it today.
This plugin closes that gap:
- **Session transcripts** — every session becomes `<dataDir>/sessions/<workspace>/<date>_<id8>.md`,

dialogue only
(user / assistant text), each message carrying a `sessionId#seq` provenance marker. A

table index
(`sessions/INDEX.md`) and a machine-readable `sessions/index.json` are maintained alongs

ide. Sub-agent sessions
(`origin: subagent` / sessions with a `parentSession`) are worker transcript

s of a parent conversation and are
skipped, so search results stay dialogue rather than delegation p

lumbing.
- **One long-term main file** — `MEMORY.md`, the durable file you and the agent actually cu

rate.
- **Wake-up digest** — `mem_wake` returns a compact summary bounded by `wakeMaxChars`.
- **Opt
ional housekeeping** — archive stale sessions out of the way, and optionally back the data directory

up to a
git remote.
Nothing is hard-coded to a particular home directory or persona; `dataDir` is configurable.
## How it differs from DSH's built-in memory tools
DSH ships its own `memory_*` tools: small key-value notes, scoped to `project` or `user`, saved and

searched by the
agent itself. Those are for facts the agent decides are worth pinning — a preference
, a decision, a convention.
This plugin handles a different job:
| | built-in `memory_*` tools | `dsh-memory-keeper` |

| unit of memory | a short note in a key-value store | a whole session transcript + `MEMORY.md` |
|

scope | `project` / `user` | a data directory you choose |
| what you get back | notes matching a ke

yword | the original dialogues, with file + line provenance |
| lifecycle | written when the agent d
ecides | exported on a timer, archived when old |
They solve different problems and are happy to coexist — the tool names differ (`mem_*` vs `memory_*

`), so installing
this plugin does not shadow or conflict with the built-in ones.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
> Not on npm yet. `dsh plugin add dsh-memory-keeper` will fail with `404 Not Found` until it is publ

ished;
> use one of the two forms above.
The plugin declares `dsh.bundle`, so the profile just has to list the package in `dsh.profile.bundle

s`. Restart the
profile afterwards (or reload it) and the `mem_*` tools appear.
Then open **Settings → Plugins → Cross-session memory** and point it at a data directory, or leave t

hat empty and
accept the default.
## The four tools
### `mem_wake`
No arguments. Returns the "what happened while you were away" digest: data directory, last export ti

me, read/write
mode, the first `wakeEntries` items of `MEMORY.md`, the last three days of diary titl

es, and the recent session
index — all capped at `wakeMaxChars` characters.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
### `mem_search`
Searches the data directory and returns hits with file, line number and the matching text. `scope` i

s
`all` | `memory` | `diary` | `sessions`.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
### `mem_write`
Writes to the main file or to today's diary. `target` is `memory` (default) | `diary`; `mode` is `ap

pend`
(default) or `replace-section` (which requires `section`); `section` names the heading to repl

ace. A `.bak` copy is
made before the write, and only the targeted section (or the end of the diary)

is touched — never a full rewrite.
The result reports bytes and sha256 before/after so you can veri

fy. Refused when `writable` is `false`. Optional
`note` says why you are writing (plugin log only, n

ot stored in the main file), `withDate` controls the date suffix
on single-line entries (default `tr
ue`), and `day` picks the diary date (default today).
[代码示例省略，未执行]
### `mem_status`
No arguments. Returns the current state: data directory and where it came from, mode (read-only / re

ad-write), main
file size and mtime, diary and session counts, last export / archive / backup times,
and the effective config.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Memory graph
`lib/assoc.mjs` is the part of this plugin that lets memories find each other: seed matching → keywo

rd overlap →
one-hop diffusion. It surfaces in two places:
- after `mem_write`, the result carries a `suggestLinks` list (plus a short `hint`) with the `[[keys
m_search` returns a `related` field: entries you can reach by following graph edges, i.e. further th

an plain
keyword matches.
[该节后续省略]
## Privacy
Session transcripts contain the full conversation content. By default everything stays on your local

disk under
`dataDir`. Do not put `dataDir` inside a public repository, and if you enable the GitHub

backup, remember you are
pushing your conversations to that remote — leave it empty unless you are
comfortable with that.
## Requirements
| piece | what |

| DSH | 0.2.x, on a profile that can install plugins |
| Node.js | >= 22 |
